s: The fall from a peak to the next low. It shows how much you could have lost, not where you ended.
cap: Drawdown: the fall from a peak to the next low. It tells you how much you could have lost along the way, not where you ended up. Chart: synthetic demo data.

s: Two series can end in the same place and feel nothing alike on the way.
cap: Two paths can end at the same number and feel nothing alike on the way. That is why drawdown and path matter, not only the final return. Chart: synthetic demo data.

s: Many possible paths from the same assumptions. Read the range, not one line.
cap: A market simulation runs many possible paths from the same assumptions. The useful output is the range, not any single line. Chart: synthetic demo data.

s: An onchain token designed to track a listed share. How it tracks varies by issuer.
cap: Tokenized stocks are onchain tokens designed to track a listed share. How they track it varies by issuer, which research on onchain finance has to account for.

s: A fund that holds a basket of assets, so one position gives you the whole basket.
cap: An ETF is a fund that holds a basket of assets, so a single position gives you exposure to the basket. Look inside the basket before you look at the label. Illustration: synthetic.
Every simulation inherits its assumptions: the time window, the return distribution, the rebalancing rule, the cost model. Change one and the answer moves. Read them first.

items: Volatility|How much returns swing around their average.
Drawdown|How far the path fell from its peak.
cap: Volatility: how much returns swing around their average. Drawdown: how far the path fell from its peak. Related, not the same. A calm-looking series can still have a deep drawdown.

s: A 50% fall needs a 100% gain to get back to even.
cap: The arithmetic of drawdowns: a 50% fall needs a 100% gain to get back to even. Depth matters, and so does the climb back. Illustration: synthetic demo data.

s: Return is a destination. Drawdown is the journey.
cap: Our view: one number hides the path. Return is a destination; drawdown is the journey. Ask for both.

h: A backtest is a story. Read the assumptions.
cap: Our view: a backtest is a story told with the benefit of hindsight. Read the assumptions behind it before you trust the ending.

h: Synthetic data is fine, if it says so.
cap: Our view: synthetic data is a fine way to explain a method, as long as it says so. Every chart in this series is labelled.

s: Reply with A, B, C or D.
cap: Community question: you are comparing two strategies. Which number do you check first? A) Max drawdown B) Recovery time C) Volatility D) Final return.

h: How long could you sit through a drawdown?
s: Honest answers only. Reply A to D.
cap: How long could you sit through a drawdown before you act? A) Days B) Weeks C) Months D) Years. The answer says more about a strategy than its average return.

h: Which would you trust for tail risk?
s: Reply with A, B, C or D.
cap: Tail risk: which do you trust more? A) Historical data B) Simulated paths C) Both D) Neither. Tell us what would change your mind.

s: Hypothetical. Run many paths, then read the worst ones before the average.
cap: Use case (hypothetical): stress-testing a basket of tokenized ETFs. Run many paths, then read the worst of them before the average. Chart: synthetic demo data.

s: Hypothetical. Same final number: compare the path, the drawdown and the assumptions.
cap: Use case (hypothetical): two strategies end with the same return. Compare the path, the drawdown and the assumptions, not just the final number. Chart: synthetic demo data.
